correctness.rationale: Independent recomputation from stored CSVs and vendored TW1 CDF reproduces all essential numbers exactly: KS_classical 0.089543/0.070261/0.046639 and KS_calibrated 0.007335/0.003677/0.008268 for N=10/20/50 match to 6 decimals; DKW epsilons sqrt(ln(40)/2n)=0.019206 (n=5000) and 0.009603 (n=20000) verified; classical mu_N=2sqrt(N) and sigma_N=N^{-1/6} verified; TW1 CDF is monotone on [-8,8] with F(-8)~2e-12, F(8)=1.0, quantiles 10% -2.782, 50% -1.268, 90% 0.451 and moments mean -1.20653365/var 1.60778073/skew 0.293461/kurt 0.165220 matching literature -1.20653357/1.60778103/0.29346/~0.16524 to ~1e-06; convergence h=0.001 vs 0.002 maxdiff 1.04e-07 negligible vs KS 1e-03. Sampler convention diag N(0,2)/chi with mu=2sqrt(N) is self-consistent for GOE edge; means 5.32464/8.08374/13.43151 reproduced; first-draw replay matches stored CSV to ~1-3e-13 (CSV 12-dec rounding) and full 500-prefix in-memory replay is deterministic with maxdiff 0.0 <1e-10 threshold (independent CSV-roundtrip replay gives 5e-13, still PASS). Classical-scaled moments and bootstrap structure reproduced (means -1.467678/-1.417773/-1.363955, vars, skews). Calibrated offsets -0.14/-0.12/-0.07 and factors 1.040/1.010/1.005 shrink with N as claimed and optimum is sharp (perturbations +0.01 in mu or +0.005 in sigma raise KS to ~0.008). Split-half check on N=20 (fit in-sample) gives half-sample KS ~0.012/0.010 vs classical ~0.065, so 19x improvement far exceeds DKW and is robust despite disclosed in-sample optimism. Histogram totals 5000/19998/5000: N=20 missing 2 counts are the two scaled samples >4 (max 5.27) outside [-6,4] bins, correctly excluded; DRAFT truncation disclosure is adequate. No proof is claimed; empirical claims are conditional on logged numpy 1.26.4/mpmath 1.2.1/Python 3.12.3, correctly scoped.

originality.rationale: Live retrieval (Crossref + arXiv, 2026-09-07) confirms none of the nearest prior results publishes the same fixed-seed finite-N GOE edge KS census with calibrated constants and replay log. Dumitriu-Edelman (2002) proves the tridiagonal beta=1 sampler construction reused here but contains no TW1 KS-distance table, no fitted mu*/sigma*, and no N=10/20/50 histogram/moment census. Tracy-Widom (1996) defines the TW1 limit via Painleve-II/Airy kernel asymptotically with no finite-N empirical calibration. Johnstone-Ma (2012, DOI 10.1214/11-AAP819) is the closest finite-N work: it proves improved centering/scaling rate bounds for GOE/GUE edge convergence but publishes no fixed-seed Dumitriu-Edelman census, no KS table at N=10/20/50, and no eigvalsh replay log. Bornemann (arXiv:2403.07628) derives analytic finite-size asymptotic expansions as derivatives of F_beta with tuned scalings and checks against large-sample simulations, which is the analytic counterpart; it does not publish a citable fixed-seed KS table with DKW bands, bootstrap moment CIs, and bit-replay log of the kind claimed. Delta is therefore the replayable empirical artifact itself, not a theorem, and no retrieved source anticipates or duplicates it.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later as a replayable sampler benchmark, not a textbook restatement or mere N-substitution. Classical edge scaling at N=10-50 is still 0.047-0.090 away from TW1 in KS (2-7x DKW epsilon), quantifying that textbook TW1 limit is not yet accurate at these N; calibrated two-parameter finite-size correction reduces KS to 0.004-0.008 (inside DKW), with shrinking offsets/factors documenting the correction trend. Fixed SeedSequence(500020), 30000 eigvalsh draws, vendored Painleve-II TW1 CDF with 1e-07 convergence proof, DKW bands, 50-bin histogram, three-moment table with 1000-bootstrap CIs, and 500-sample replay log together give downstream RMT/statistics/numerical-linear-algebra users a concrete <2min rerunnable reference for tridiagonal sampler correctness and edge-scaling choice. Gain is large (up to 19x), motivated, and honestly caveated as in-sample; limitations (N range, one seed family/convention, no analytic rate proof) are disclosed. Passes motivated/substantive gates; would be cited as a calibration check, not as a new law.
